title: Beyond Carrier or Competitor: Microplastics as Dynamic Mediators of PFAS Fate, Bioavailability, and Remediation
content: Microplastics (MPs) and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) increasingly co-occur across aquatic, terrestrial, and biological systems, yet single-pollutant frameworks poorly represent their interactions. This review resolves whether MPs function as carriers that enhance PFAS mobility and bioavailability or as competitors that reduce freely dissolved PFAS through sorption. The evidence reveals a dynamic, context-dependent continuum governed by polymer identity, PFAS chemistry, environmental aging, biofilm development, and water chemistry. Pristine MPs can promote PFAS transport through hydrophobic partitioning and colloid-mediated mobility, whereas oxidation and colonisation may increase surface functionality, strengthening sorption and temporary sequestration. Because sorption is reversible, environmental or biological changes can trigger desorption, remobilisation, and exposure. Machine-learning approaches could help predict these multidimensional interactions, but models coupling MP and PFAS properties remain scarce. The carrier–competitor paradigm further supports integrated remediation combining phase-resolved characterisation, simultaneous capture, contaminant recovery, media regeneration, and PFAS destruction. Overall, MPs should be treated as dynamic mediators of PFAS fate within transformation-aware, mixture-based frameworks for exposure assessment, risk prediction, and remediation design.
